text:
Jumping or intermittent rotary motion, used for meters and revolution-counters. The drop and attached pawl, carried by a spring at the left, are lifted by pins in the disk at the right. Pins escape first from pawl, which drops into next space of the star-wheel. When pin escapes from drop, spring throws down suddenly the drop, the pin on which strikes the pawl, which, by its action on star-wheel, rapidly gives it a portion of a revolution. This is repeated as each pin passes.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 63
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 63; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_063.html.

text:
The left-hand disk or wheel, C, is the driving-wheel, upon which is fixed the tappet, A. The other disk or wheel, D, has a series of equidistant studs projecting from its face. Every rotation of the tappet acting upon one of the studs in the wheel, D, causes the latter wheel to move the distance of one stud.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 65
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 65; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_065.html.

text:
Continuous rotary converted into intermittent rotary motion. The disk-wheel, B, carrying the stops, C, D, turns on a center eccentric to the cam, A. On continuous rotary motion being given to the cam, A, intermittent rotary motion is imparted to the wheel, B. The stops free themselves from the offset of the cam at every half-revolution, the wheel, B, remaining at rest until the cam has completed its revolution, when the same motion is repeated.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 88
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 88; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_088.html.
